statements.statement: A member said the school budget gap was just shy of $1 million last year and $2 million this year.
The citizens petition sought a Proposition 2½ override to fund the schools' shortfall.
A member estimated the override would add roughly $400 to the average tax bill versus a larger, costlier override.
The board recommended a warrant article transferring $500,000 in certified free cash to the schools' FY26 budget, but only if the override fails.
The assistant town manager said a 3% COLA for SAP employees would cost about $43,46, roughly $7,300 more than the budgeted 2.5% COLA.
A member noted the school department budget had grown about 13% over the last two years.

warnings.condition: if the override does not pass
warnings.prediction: The $2 million shortfall was described as equating to the loss of more than 20 teaching positions.

warnings.about: size and passability of a future override
warnings.condition: if the district needs a multi-year or larger override next year
warnings.prediction: A future override could need to be much larger (discussion referenced up to $5 million), which the member feared voters would reject outright.

warnings.condition: in exchange for a townwide override being pursued next year
warnings.prediction: The fire union said it would forgo pursuing its fourth shift for another year to allow room for a broader townwide override.

warnings.condition: if presented without adequate planning and public education
warnings.prediction: Voters could say no to a large multi-year override if it is not paired with a clear, vetted, well-communicated plan.
